lesson.grammar_point: how about and what about + noun or -ing (making and answering offers)

listenings.text: Good morning, and welcome to the store. This week every coat and every pair of jeans is on sale, so this is a very good week for a bargain. If something does not fit, you can bring it back within thirty days. Please keep the tag on the item, and bring the receipt with you: that is our return policy. Without the receipt we can only offer you an exchange, never a refund. If an item is faulty, come straight to the counter on the ground floor, and we will change it for you on the same day. Thank you for shopping with us, and enjoy your morning.

Yesterday I found a leather bag at the market, and the price on the tag was sixty euros. That was too much for me, so I looked at the man and I asked him: how about forty? He laughed and he said fifty. Then I said: what about forty-five, and I take two of them? He thought about it for a second, and he said yes. That was a real bargain. Later I went back to the clothes store, because the shirt I bought for my wife was the wrong size. The woman at the counter looked at my receipt and asked me one question: a refund, or an exchange? I chose the exchange, and I did all of it in English.

extra_audio.text: First, Roberto sees a leather bag at the market and looks at the price on the tag. Then he makes an offer: how about forty euros? Next, the seller says fifty, and Roberto suggests forty-five for two bags. After that, the seller shakes his hand and Roberto walks away with a real bargain. Finally, he goes back to the clothes store with the receipt, and he exchanges the shirt for a larger size.

reading.rtitle: Two kinds of price, two kinds of rule
paras: In most European stores the price on the tag is the price you pay. Nobody haggles in a supermarket, and nobody haggles in a big clothes shop. But in an open-air market, at a flea market, or in a small souvenir shop, the price on the tag is only a starting point, and the seller expects you to make an offer. One short question opens the whole conversation: how about a better price if I take two?

Haggling is not a fight. You stay friendly, you smile, and you make one offer at a time. If the seller says no, you can try again in other words: what about meeting in the middle? Many sellers also give a small discount for cash. And if the price does not move, you say thank you and you walk away. That is a normal end to a conversation in a market, and nobody is offended.

A store is a different world. There the rule is the return policy, and every store prints it on the receipt. In the European Union a faulty item is always your right: if the thing you bought does not work, the store must repair it, exchange it, or give you a refund. But if you simply do not like the color, that is not a fault, and the store decides. Most big shops still take the item back for thirty days, with the tag on it and the receipt in your hand.

Online is more generous. When you buy on the internet you have fourteen days to change your mind, and you do not have to explain why. So the bargain you find in a market and the shirt you buy online follow two different sets of rules, and it is worth knowing which one you are in. Either way, one sentence opens the door in any shop: excuse me, what is your return policy?
